result.summary: This is the tenant's own job: tidying the front garden after it was raised at inspection. In their latest email (event 013) the tenant says it will be finished this evening and they'll send photos tomorrow morning. Nothing needs to be done until those photos are due. The old hold had no follow-up date, so I replaced it with one that chases in 2 days. I did not message the tenant because they had just told us what they would do next.
result.situation: The front garden at Flat 4, 174 Beacon Close needed tidying after the inspection. The tenant was chased by email on 1, 8 (sent twice), 20 and 26 Feb, and by phone on 13 Feb. Their family member had been in hospital (event 007). On 26 Feb at 10:39 the tenant replied that the work will be finished that evening and photos will follow the next morning. The ticket is at intake and was on hold with no follow-up date.

judgement.why_this_decision: The tenant's reply (event 013) gives a specific completion time and says when the photos will arrive. The classifier rated it routine (autonomy auto, safety 0.02). The next step is the tenant's and nothing is overdue yet, so the right move is a hold with a firm follow-up date. There is no contractor or landlord money involved, so no approval is needed.

alternatives_considered.option: Send the tenant an acknowledgement or another chaser
alternatives_considered.why_not: The tenant has just told us what they will do and when. Another message would add nothing; the hold covers the chase.
The tenant has now replied and committed to a time, so they are not unresponsive.
The work hasn't been confirmed as done and no photos have been received.
